Zava, Inc. — AI Procurement Playbook v.2.1 | ZAVA-LEGAL-PB-AI-2.1 | CONFIDENTIAL
ZAVA, INC.
AI PROCUREMENT PLAYBOOK v.2.1
Document Reference: ZAVA-LEGAL-PB-AI-2.1 Effective Date: June 1, 2026 Classification: Internal — Attorney-Client Privileged / Work Product Prepared by: Office of the Associate General Counsel — Technology Transactions
Attorney-client privileged work product. Distribution limited to authorized Zava, Inc. personnel.
COVER MEMORANDUM
TO: Zava Legal — Technology Transactions; Procurement; Information Security; Product & AI Strategy (Hemanti Baishya, VP); Chief Underwriting Officer (Luc Lacombe)
FROM: Emil Vanggaard, Associate General Counsel — Technology Transactions
This Playbook sets Zava, Inc.'s ("Zava" or the "Company") mandatory positions, fallbacks, risk ratings, and approval thresholds for all agreements with artificial intelligence and machine learning vendors. Compliance is mandatory.
Risk Context. Zava uses third-party AI in regulated insurance underwriting. The Colorado Division of Insurance and the New York Department of Financial Services are scrutinizing AI-driven underwriting, and Zava's EU expansion brings the GDPR and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act), under which insurance AI is high-risk.
Playbook Owner. Emil Vanggaard, Associate General Counsel — Technology Transactions, may approve exceptions to any non-hard-stop position, subject to Section 13.
SECTION 1 — SCOPE & DEFINITIONS
1.1 Scope.  This Playbook applies to every AI/ML vendor agreement, order, pilot, amendment, and renewal, on the vendor's paper or Zava's. On vendor paper, mark up the form to the Required Positions or document approved fallbacks.
1.2 Defined Terms. "ACV" means Total Contract Value divided by the years of the initial term (e.g., $14,750,000 over five years is an ACV of $2,950,000).
"Company Data" means all data Zava provides or generates through the Platform, including derivatives, inferences, and outputs produced from it.
"Fine-Tuned Model Weights" means model parameters adjusted or trained using Company Data, as distinct from the vendor's base models.
"Material Model Change" means any model change that causes greater than two percent (2%) variance in output distribution against an agreed validation set, or any change to training-data sources.
"Model Card" means a document describing a model's intended use, performance, training data and provenance, limitations, bias results, and version history, consistent with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF).
"Outputs/Inferences" means all scores, predictions, and other results the Platform generates from Company Data.
"Platform" means the vendor's AI/ML software, models, and infrastructure provided under the agreement.
"Security Incident" means any unauthorized access to, acquisition, use, disclosure, destruction, or loss of Company Data, whether or not harm results.
1.3 Playbook Structure — How to Use This Document. Each topic in Sections 2–12 states a Required Position, an acceptable Fallback, and a risk rating for deviation (Critical, High, Medium, or Low). Approvals follow Section 13 and are recorded in the negotiation tracker. Positions marked [HARD STOP] have no fallback (Section 14).
SECTION 2 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY & DATA OWNERSHIP
2.1 Fine-Tuned Model Weights. Required Position: Zava owns, or co-owns with full independent rights, all Fine-Tuned Model Weights, delivered in a portable format (e.g., ONNX) within thirty (30) days of request and on termination. Fallback: a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license, exclusive within insurance, with portability. Risk: Critical (Business Priority #1; deviation requires joint approval by Emil Vanggaard and Hemanti Baishya).
2.2 Outputs and Inferences. Required Position: all Outputs/Inferences are Zava's sole and exclusive property. The vendor may use them only as strictly necessary to perform the services during the term and may not otherwise retain, analyze, aggregate, or de-identify them. Fallback: None. [HARD STOP] Risk: Critical.
2.3 Vendor Use of Company Data for Cross-Customer Model Improvement. Required Position: no use of Company Data to train or improve models for other customers or general-purpose models without Zava's prior written, opt-in consent for each use, revocable at any time. Delete generic "service improvement" clauses. Fallback: only fully de-identified, aggregated metadata, with an opt-out. Risk: Critical.
2.4 Pre-Existing and Background IP. Required Position: the vendor keeps its base models and pre-existing IP, but Zava receives a perpetual license to any of it needed to use the Fine-Tuned Model Weights. Fallback: a term-limited license, if the weights are confirmed portable without it. Risk: High.
SECTION 3 — DATA PROTECTION & PRIVACY
3.1 Applicable Privacy Laws. Required Position: the vendor warrants compliance with the CCPA/CPRA (as service provider), the GDPR (as processor, under an Article 28 data processing agreement), the Colorado Privacy Act, and the EU AI Act provider obligations for high-risk AI, and notifies Zava within ten (10) business days of any regulatory inquiry or change in compliance status. Fallback: GDPR compliance within ninety (90) days, with no EU data processed until then. Risk: Critical (CCPA, GDPR); High (Colorado Privacy Act, EU AI Act).
3.2 Algorithmic Audits. Required Position: Zava may conduct, or commission an independent third party to conduct, an algorithmic audit at least annually covering accuracy, bias, training data, explainability, and regulatory compliance, with the vendor's full cooperation. The vendor pays for the first annual audit and any audit triggered by a Security Incident, compliance concern, or regulatory inquiry. Fallback: an annual audit by a mutually agreed independent auditor, with the full report shared within thirty (30) days. Risk: Critical.
3.3 Bias Testing. Required Position: quarterly bias testing across protected classes, with a written report and remediation plan within fifteen (15) business days. Fallback: semi-annual testing plus ad hoc testing on request. Risk: Critical.
3.4 Model Cards. Required Position: a Model Card for every model version, delivered before deployment. Fallback: equivalent documentation within ten (10) business days of release. Risk: High.
3.5 Explainability — NIST AI RMF. Required Position: explainability consistent with the NIST AI RMF "Measure" function, including decision-level explanations within five (5) business days of request. Fallback: feature-importance or SHAP explanations plus a twelve-month roadmap to full alignment. Risk: High.
3.6 Data Lineage & Training-Data Provenance. Required Position: representations on the lineage and provenance of all training data, including sources, legal basis, and chain of custody, and that no data was obtained unlawfully. Fallback: a provenance attestation plus an indemnity for training-data claims. Risk: High.
3.7 Security Incident Response — Data Protection Overlay. Required Position: notice of any Security Incident within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery (and in time for Zava's seventy-two (72) hour GDPR deadline), with full cooperation and no public statement without consent. Fallback: seventy-two (72) hours from discovery, with a preliminary notice within twenty-four (24) hours. Risk: Critical.
SECTION 4 — SECURITY & AUDIT
4.1 SOC 2 Reports. Required Position: an annual SOC 2 Type II report covering at least twelve (12) months, delivered within ninety (90) days of the audit period end. A SOC 2 Type I report is not sufficient. Fallback: a Type II report within one hundred eighty (180) days of the effective date, with enhanced audit rights meanwhile. Risk: Critical.
4.2 Penetration Testing. Required Position: Zava may conduct or commission an annual penetration test on thirty (30) days' notice; critical and high findings remediated within thirty (30) days. Fallback: an annual vendor-commissioned independent test with the full report shared. Risk: High.
4.3 On-Site / Remote Audit Rights. Required Position: on-site or remote audits once per year on fifteen (15) business days' notice, plus ad hoc audits after a Security Incident or regulatory inquiry. Fallback: once per year unless an incident or inquiry occurs; results may be shared with regulators. Risk: High.
SECTION 5 — LIABILITY
5.1 General Liability Cap. Required Position: a general liability cap of at least two times (2×) ACV ($5,900,000 for a $2,950,000 ACV). Fallback: eighteen (18) months' fees as an absolute floor. Risk: Critical.
5.2 Super-Cap (Enhanced Liability Categories). Required Position: a Super-Cap of three times (3×) ACV ($8,850,000) for intellectual property infringement, data breach, and breach of confidentiality. Fallback: 2.5× ACV ($7,375,000), only if the general cap is 2× ACV. Risk: Critical.
5.3 Uncapped Liability Categories. Required Position: uncapped liability for fraud or intentional misrepresentation, willful misconduct or gross negligence, and the vendor's third-party IP indemnity. Fallback: None. [HARD STOP] Risk: Critical.
5.4 Vendor Liability Cap Benchmarks. Vendor caps of six (6) or twelve (12) months' fees must be rejected. On a $2,950,000 ACV ($2,710,000 platform fee), a six-month cap is about $1,355,000 (half the platform fee) or $1,475,000 (half of ACV), against $5,900,000 under the Required Position.
SECTION 6 — INDEMNIFICATION
6.1 Intellectual Property Indemnification. Required Position: the vendor indemnifies Zava against third-party claims that the Platform infringes any patent, copyright, trade secret, trademark, or other intellectual property right, with a cure, replace, or refund remedy. Fallback: U.S. claims only, extended to the EU if EU data is processed. Risk: Critical.
6.2 AI Output Indemnity. Required Position: an AI Output indemnity covering third-party claims that Outputs/Inferences infringe intellectual property rights or are defamatory. Fallback: limited to Outputs of the vendor's base models. Risk: High.
6.3 Indemnification Procedures. Prompt notice is required, but delay excuses the indemnifier only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifier controls the defense through counsel reasonably acceptable to Zava, which may participate with its own counsel. No settlement may impose obligations, admissions, or non-monetary relief on Zava without its consent.
SECTION 7 — INSURANCE
7.1 Required Minimum Coverage. Required Position: Vendor maintains the following minimum coverage during the term and for twenty-four (24) months after:
Coverage Type
Minimum Per Claim / Per Occurrence
Minimum Aggregate
Commercial General Liability (CGL)
$5,000,000
$5,000,000
Errors & Omissions / Technology Professional Indemnity (E&O/Tech PI)
$10,000,000
$10,000,000
Cyber Liability / Network Security & Privacy Insurance
$10,000,000
$10,000,000
AI-Specific E&O Rider
$5,000,000
$5,000,000
Fallback: CGL $3,000,000 if the vendor's balance sheet covers the gap; E&O/Tech PI $10,000,000 is non-negotiable for ACV of $2,000,000 or more; Cyber $5,000,000 with equivalent self-insurance; AI-Specific E&O Rider $3,000,000, rising to $5,000,000 within twelve (12) months. Risk: Critical (Cyber, AI-Specific E&O Rider); High (CGL, E&O/Tech PI).
7.2 Additional Insurance Requirements. Insurers must be rated A- or better by A.M. Best. Zava must be an additional insured on CGL and Cyber policies, with certificates on execution and renewal, thirty (30) days' notice of cancellation, waiver of subrogation, and primary, non-contributory coverage.
SECTION 8 — FEES & ESCALATION
8.1 Fee Escalator Cap. Required Position: annual escalators may not exceed CPI (U.S. City Average) plus one percentage point (CPI + 1%), with a hard cap of three percent (3%) a year and no increase in year one. Reject five percent (5%) compounding escalators. Fallback: CPI + 1.5%, capped at 4%, only with a five percent (5%) reduction in the year-one fee. Risk: High.
8.2 Fee Escalator — Illustration of Impact. On a $2,710,000 platform fee, a five percent (5%) compounding escalator totals $14,974,461 over five years, against $14,387,358 under CPI + 1% capped at 3%: about $587,000 more.
8.3 Overage Fees. Overage rates and the monthly volume threshold (e.g., 4,000,000 decisions) must be fixed for the term, with no downward adjustment, and unused volume should roll over or earn a credit. At $0.018 per decision, 4,500,000 decisions in a month cost $9,000 in overage.
8.4 Service Level Credits and Fee Remedies. Required Position: 99.5% monthly availability with tiered service credits; a credit cap of 5% of monthly fees (about $11,292) is a floor, and deals over $2,000,000 ACV should seek 10%. Fallback: a 5% cap only with a no-penalty termination right if availability falls below 99.0% for three (3) consecutive months or below 95.0% in any month. Risk: Medium (credit cap); High (termination right).
SECTION 9 — MODEL GOVERNANCE & CHANGE CONTROL
9.1 Material Model Changes — Notice and Approval. Required Position: at least sixty (60) calendar days' written notice before any Material Model Change, and Zava's prior written approval, which Zava may withhold for any reason, before deployment. Fallback: forty-five (45) days' notice plus a right to revert to the prior version within thirty (30) days, at the vendor's cost. Risk: Critical. Vendor forms often allow fifteen (15) days' notice with no approval right; escalate to Emil Vanggaard and Luc Lacombe.
9.2 Deprecated Models — Continued Availability. Required Position: a deprecated model version stays fully available and supported for at least twelve (12) months after notice, at no extra cost, with migration support. Fallback: nine (9) months, extendable by three (3). Risk: High.
9.3 Model Versioning and Documentation. The vendor maintains a version history for every model (changes, training data, performance metrics, Model Card, and bias results for each Material Model Change), retained for seven (7) years after termination.
SECTION 10 — SUBCONTRACTING
10.1 Consent Requirements. Required Position: no subcontracting of model training or fine-tuning, processing or storage of Company Data, or hosting without Zava's prior written consent. Fallback: pre-approved hosting subcontractors listed in an exhibit; training and data processing always need consent. Risk: Critical (training, data processing); High (hosting).
10.2 Subcontractor Liability Flow-Down. Required Position: the vendor is fully liable for its subcontractors at all tiers as if their acts were its own, with flow-down terms at least as protective of Zava. Fallback: None. [HARD STOP] Risk: Critical.
10.3 Subcontractor List Maintenance. Required Position: a current subcontractor list attached as a formal exhibit (not inside an acceptable use policy), updated within five (5) business days of any change. Fallback: updates within ten (10) business days, with a right to object. Risk: Medium.
SECTION 11 — TERMINATION & TRANSITION
11.1 Transition Period. Required Position: a transition period of at least one hundred eighty (180) days after termination for any reason, with full services at current fees and service levels. Fallback: one hundred twenty (120) days, only with the transition services in Section 11.3. Risk: Critical. A ninety (90)-day wind-down must be rejected.
11.2 Data Return. Required Position: all Company Data, including Fine-Tuned Model Weights and Outputs/Inferences, returned in Apache Parquet or CSV within thirty (30) calendar days of termination notice, with a data dictionary and certified deletion afterward. Proprietary formats are not acceptable. Fallback: another open format (e.g., JSON) Zava agrees to in advance. Proprietary-only return is a [HARD STOP]. Risk: Critical.
11.3 Transition Services. Required Position: transition services for up to twelve (12) months after termination at no more than one hundred ten percent (110%) of then-current fees, including knowledge transfer, API access, and cooperation with a successor. Fallback: six (6) months at 120%, extendable six (6) months at 130%. Risk: High.
11.4 Source-Code Escrow. Required Position: source-code escrow with Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc., updated annually and on each major release, released on vendor insolvency, uncured material breach, or discontinuation of the Platform, with a perpetual internal-use license to the released materials. Fallback: another nationally recognized escrow agent with the same release triggers. Risk: Critical.
11.5 Anti-Lock-In Principles. Zava must never be locked in to a single AI vendor. Flag proprietary formats, exclusivity, exit penalties, late-notice auto-renewals, and migration fees for negotiation or deletion.
SECTION 12 — GOVERNING LAW & DISPUTE RESOLUTION
12.1 Governing Law. Required Position: Delaware law. Fallback: New York law. Vendor home-state law (e.g., Texas) needs Emil Vanggaard's approval. Risk: High.
12.2 Dispute Resolution — Forum. Required Position: exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware Court of Chancery (or Superior Court) or the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. Fallback: the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, with New York law. Risk: High.
12.3 No Mandatory Arbitration. Required Position: no mandatory binding arbitration (JAMS, AAA, ICC, or otherwise); delete any arbitration clause. Fallback: None. [HARD STOP] Risk: Critical.
12.4 No Class-Action Waiver. Required Position: no class-action, collective-action, or representative-action waiver. Fallback: None. [HARD STOP] Risk: Critical.
12.5 Jury-Trial Waiver. A mutual jury-trial waiver is acceptable; a waiver binding only Zava is not. Risk: Low.
SECTION 13 — DECISION MATRIX — ESCALATION THRESHOLDS BY ACV BAND
Approval of fallbacks and deviations depends on the engagement's ACV band. No band permits a hard-stop deviation.
13.1 ACV Bands
•  Band 1 (ACV below $500,000): the Senior Associate approves Fallbacks; anything below a Fallback needs the Associate General Counsel.
•  Band 2 (ACV $500,000–$2,000,000): the Associate General Counsel approves all Fallbacks and Critical or High deviations.
•  Band 3 (ACV $2,000,001–$5,000,000): the Associate General Counsel approves all Fallbacks and High deviations; Critical deviations need joint approval by the Associate General Counsel and the VP of Product & AI Strategy.
•  Band 4 (ACV above $5,000,000): the General Counsel approves all Fallbacks and any Medium or Low deviation; Critical or High deviations need the General Counsel, the VP of Product & AI Strategy, and the CFO.
13.2 Current Trey Research Engagement Classification. The Trey Research engagement (ACV $2,950,000; TCV $14,750,000 over five years) is Band 3. Critical deviations need joint approval by Emil Vanggaard and Hemanti Baishya; High deviations and all Fallbacks need Emil Vanggaard. Record every deviation in the negotiation tracker.
SECTION 14 — HARD STOPS — NON-NEGOTIABLE POSITIONS
A hard stop may not be conceded under any circumstances. If a vendor refuses one, escalate to the General Counsel for a proceed/no-proceed decision.
1.  Zava's sole ownership of Outputs/Inferences (Section 2.2).
2.  Uncapped liability for fraud or intentional misrepresentation, willful misconduct or gross negligence, and third-party IP indemnity (Section 5.3).
3.  Full vendor liability for subcontractors, with protective flow-downs (Section 10.2).
4.  No mandatory binding arbitration (Section 12.3).
5.  No class-action waiver (Section 12.4).
6.  Data return in open, non-proprietary formats (Section 11.2).
SECTION 15 — APPROVAL
APPROVED:

Title: Associate General Counsel — Technology Transactions
Date: June 1, 2026
